title: Patch rollback and dependency compatibility checklist (scratchpad)
notes:
Context:
Small-but-risky change touching batching router + legacy config parsing. Observed flakiness on staging: intermittent 5xxs during high concurrency runs (simulated via load script). PR touches fast-path for split-batching and introduces a new optional header that some older clients don't send.

Why this doc: personal scratchpad for reviewing PR, thinking through rollback/backport and safe merge gating. Keep short, copy to PR description if we converge.

Quick checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Confirm unit tests cover header absent case (parser defaulting). File: router/config_parser_test.go -> add case if missing.
- [ ] Add deterministic integration test that runs split-batching with clients not sending header (CI slow but required). Tag as integration:long.
- [ ] Run canary on dedicated pool with 10% traffic for 24h. Watch error budget and p50/p99 tail.
- [ ] Validate metrics naming backwards compatibility (old dashboards expect metric names unchanged).
- [ ] Verify no new DB migrations / schema changes. If so, add migration rollback script.
- [ ] Confirm no change to tokenization or KV cache format (if yes, block).

Observed failure modes to test for (notes):
- spikes of 502 during batching boundary transitions (likely race in router queue length calc). Repro steps below.
- some internal clients (mobile-dev) hit 415 when header missing -> parsing path returns bad request for older agent versions.

Repro steps (local/staging):
1) Start local runtime with --staging-config and reduced batching thresholds.
2) Run load script scripts/loaders/split_batch_test.py with 500 concurrent clients, half of them simulating old-client (no header).
3) Observe logs: look for "batch-boundary-update" lines within 200ms windows and correlate with 502s.
4) Enable debug logging for router/queue and collect flame scope if latency jumps.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- Immediate: revert the merge commit (git revert -m 1 <merge_sha>) and deploy hotfix job to canary then prod.
- If revert fails because subsequent PRs depend on this change: deploy compatibility shim that accepts missing header and falls back to old behavior (small patch) and promote.
- Communicate to SRE Slack channel and set incident channel if >1% error rate over 5m window.

Backport plan (if merge required for stable branch):
- Identify minimal subset: parser default + compatibility tests.
- Backport target: release/2026-02-stable. Avoid bringing batching optimization changes into stable branch.
- Create backport PR with label backport/stable and link original PR.

Manual verification checklist (post-deploy canary):
- Verify p50/p90/p99 latencies for serviced routes (per-route dashboard).
- Run small synthetic: 100 requests/s with 40% old-client. Confirm zero 4xx/5xx related to parsing.
- Check logs for header-related warnings. Search for "unknown-client-header" occurrences (should be zero).

Risk matrix quick map:
- Parser fallback missing -> moderate impact, targeted errors for some clients.
- Batching race -> high impact, spikes across many customers -> requires immediate rollback.
- Metrics break -> low-medium, observability degraded but system still runs.

Tests to add/adjust (dev notes):
- unit: parser_test: no-header, bad-header, extra-field.
- integration: split-batching compatibility, long-run (1h) stability test. Add to ci/integration/slow with opt-in tag.
- e2e: add behavioral test in QA harness that exercises canary promotion scripts.

PR review talking points (for reviewer checklist):
- Does the new header default to a safe value in all call sites?
- Is any behavior conditional on presence/absence of header documented in API contract?
- Are there feature flags we can flip to roll out incrementally? If not, ask author to add.
- Are new metrics emitted with a clear migration plan for dashboards?
- Where are the perf regression benchmarks? Author should include before/after numbers for p50/p99 under 95th percentile load.

Post-merge follow-ups (if merged):
- Force add canary monitor for 48h and schedule status check at 4h, 12h, 24h. Owner: Samir.
- Add a short blameless postmortem template if any rollback happened. Owner: me (Evan).
- Add note to release notes: compatibility caveat and recommended client upgrade window.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: Do any third-party partners use older client bundles that will not be able to upgrade quickly? Check CRM notes and partner-integration spreadsheet.
- Q: Does mobile-dev pipeline pin client headers? Ping Maya to check.
- TODO: Draft a small migration email for partner-facing customers describing the window and fallback behavior.
- TODO: If we decide to keep change, add a deprecation period entry and a feature flag for 3 months.

Random notes / heuristics I keep forgetting:
- Prefer adding a lightweight compatibility shim over a full revert when possible (less churn) but only if shim is cheap and well-tested.
- When reverting, explicitly mention the revert reason in the PR body so release notes are clear.
- Keep an eye on canary sample size; small canaries sometimes hide statistically significant regressions.

If/when this becomes stable: copy the final checklist to CONFLUENCE:deploy-runbooks/rollback-guides under "batching-router header compatibility" and link to GH PR and INF-2293.

End of scratchpad.

Notes-to-self: capture final checklist items and move to PR description before requesting approval.
